assignment_criteria.evidence: Production Deliver selects module_deliveries.created_by; CallContract uses the authenticated consumer id, core events/grants and mail use core. A spoofed provider_id and sender in payload do not affect the verified pusher.

Separate X-Togavsu-Sender-Signature t=,v2= HMAC over v2.<unix>.<sender>.<raw body>; original timestamped v1 header stays unchanged. Both strict sender and legacy verification pass on each actual delivery. Tampering, missing binding, duplicate headers, timestamp mismatch/expiry and empty/wrong keys fail.
VerifyWebhookSender returns only authenticated identity; SignWebhookSenderHeaders and coretest.ReadDelivery supply helpers. Real coretest DeliverEvents uses the production queue and signer.

Two providers linked; Zoom pushes payload claiming Google; duplicate push from Google preserves first pusher. First delivery refused, Zoom unlinked, persisted retry due advanced in test only. Retried sender remains Zoom and body identical. A new push after unlink fails.

MODULE-KIT, module API, API conventions, shared contract docs, generated OpenAPI and CORE-UPDATE-2E describe sender header fields, exact wire framing, compatibility and verification. API contract tests validate required sender headers and unchanged v1 schema.
